stories.headline: Bihar floods: Congress sends relief supplies to Gopalganj, Bettiah
stories.title: Bihar floods: Congress sends relief supplies to Gopalganj, Bettiah
stories.summary: Relief campaign led by Siwan Congress leader Vakil Prasad Gupta has been expanded to flood-hit areas of Gopalganj and Bettiah
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Congress has expanded its relief campaign for flood-affected families in Bihar, dispatching trucks carrying dry food and essential medicines to affected areas of Gopalganj and Bettiah on Monday.
The campaign is being led by Siwan Congress leader and social worker Vakil Prasad Gupta, who said the initiative aims to provide food and essential medical supplies to families affected by flooding.
Flooding has disrupted normal life in several areas, leaving residents in need of assistance with basic necessities and healthcare.
Earlier, Gupta and his team visited flood-affected areas of Chhapra and distributed relief supplies among families in need.
The campaign has now been extended to Gopalganj and Bettiah, where the latest consignment is scheduled to be distributed among affected residents.
Gupta said helping families affected by floods was a social responsibility and that delivering food and essential medicines to those in need remained a priority during the crisis.
He said relief supplies had been sent to Gopalganj and Bettiah following the team's earlier efforts in Chhapra.
The campaign would continue in an effort to assist families affected by the flooding, he added.
Congress district president Sushil Kumar said party workers were making continued efforts to support flood victims.
He said it was important to stand with affected communities during a disaster and provide assistance according to their needs.
The relief campaign seeks to support families struggling with the effects of the flooding, he added.

stories.headline: Bihar govt transfers Rs 112.14 crore to 1.60 lakh flood-hit families
stories.title: Bihar govt transfers Rs 112.14 crore to 1.60 lakh flood-hit families
stories.summary: On Monday, Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary transferred an ex gratia amount of Rs 7,000 each to the bank accounts of 1.60 lakh beneficiaries through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: On Monday, Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary transferred an ex gratia amount of Rs 7,000 each to the bank accounts of 1.60 lakh beneficiaries through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).
Patna: The Bihar government has disbursed Rs 112.14 crore in financial assistance to flood-affected families across the state.

During a programme at the Chief Minister’s Secretariat, Samrat Choudhary directed all District Magistrates (DMs) to promptly submit details of flood-affected families who have not yet received the assistance so that eligible beneficiaries can also be provided relief.
He announced that the agricultural input subsidy for farmers affected by the floods would be transferred to their accounts on October 14.
The assistance is intended to provide relief to farmers whose crops were damaged by the flooding.
The Chief Minister also directed officials to complete repairs to flood-damaged infrastructure before Diwali.
He stressed the need to accelerate relief and rehabilitation work to restore normalcy in affected areas as quickly as possible.
Recent flooding in the Ganga, Gandak, Kosi, Bagmati and Kamla Balan rivers has affected approximately 55 lakh people in Bihar.
Many families have suffered damage to their homes, crops and other property.
The impact remains visible in Bhagalpur, Patna, Munger, Bhojpur and Buxar districts, where erosion along the Ganga continues despite a decline in the river’s water level.
In Naugachia, several multi-storey houses have reportedly been swept into the river because of severe erosion.

Besides the Ganga basin, soil erosion also happened in the Gandak, Bagmati, Kosi, Burhi Gandak, and Kamla Balan basins and several districts like West Champaran, Gopalganj, Muzaffarpur, Sheohar, Sitamarhi, Darbhanga, and Madhunai are affected by it.

stories.headline: Poonch: 4 terrorists killed in failed infiltration bid near LoC
stories.title: Poonch: 4 terrorists killed in failed infiltration bid near LoC
stories.summary: Jammu, Oct 12 : Four terrorists, including a top commander of the Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT), were killed in a landmine explosion while attempting to infiltrate into Indian Territory near Line of Control (LoC) in Poonch district on Monday. Official sources told the news agency—Kashmir News Observer (KNO) that the incident took place in the Krishna Ghati Sector where the group was attempting to cross into this side. “Terrorists were killed after triggering a landmine,” they said, adding, “The incident foiled an infiltration attempt, with all four terrorists dying at the spot.” The identity of the slain LeT commander and the circumstances leading to the suspected infiltration attempt are being ascertained, sources said, adding that following the blast, security forces sounded an alert across the sector and stepped up vigilance along the LoC to assess the situation and prevent any potential security breach. “Blast occurred in the Satwal-Naki area near the LoC. The area is considered to be a traditional infiltration route. In the past few years, terrorists have made attempts to sneak into the Indian side of the border through the route, sources said, adding hat in the past, too, six to seven members of Pakistan's BAT team were killed in a similar manner in this area,” sources said—(KNO)

Preliminary reports suggest that a landmine went off near the Nangi Takri area on Monday (October 12, 2026) near zero line.
Casualties were feared, officials said.
“Circumstances leading to the explosion are being established,” they said.

The NIA said a search was conducted on April 6 at the residential premises and led to the detection of two suspected Pakistani terrorists, identified as Abu Huraira and Khubaib of the LeT.

stories.headline: "We will never go back to square one": Iran remains open to US nuclear talks with firm conditions
stories.title: "We will never go back to square one": Iran remains open to US nuclear talks with firm conditions
stories.summary: Tehran [Iran], October 12 : In a definitive declaration outlining Tehran’s diplomatic stance, Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei asserted that while Iran is willing to engage in nuclear negotiations with the United States, it will not reset the clock on past grievances or ignore the changing realities on the ground. Speaking on Monday against the backdrop of heightened Middle East tensions and ongoing economic sanctions, Baghaei firmly rejected the idea that diplomacy can simply return to its original baseline. "We will never go back to square one. Can you ignore the experiences of the past two years and then say that we are back to square one? Every day that passes, we will definitely use its experience, both in terms of strengthening our own capabilities and in terms of learning from the other side’s lapses," he said. Baghaei emphasised that Tehran has not walked away from the negotiating table, framing diplomacy as an integral tool alongside national defence. "We are so confident that we will never run away from the negotiating table and diplomacy. Diplomacy is as important to us as the battlefield and war. We will definitely use the tools of diplomacy, wherever necessary and wherever possible, to secure our interests," said Baghaei. However, he pointed out a direct contradiction in Western strategy, arguing that military pressure, sanctions, and economic warfare undermine the genuine spirit of negotiations. "The party that should be solely blamed and held accountable for this situation is the party that destroyed the negotiating table in the middle of the negotiations and continues to insist on its previous excesses. How can one claim to negotiate and be diplomatic, while they have escalated the economic war, have practically maintained the conditions of war, and then claim that they are seeking negotiations?" questioned Baghaei. Addressing Western anxieties over Iran’s potential departure from the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT), Baghaei noted that international inaction following attacks on Iranian peaceful nuclear infrastructure has fueled debate within the country. "Why are they worried? There is no point in worrying. They have created this concern themselves. Self-inflicted is not a tactic," he said. He added that those responsible for undermining global non-proliferation norms must be held accountable. "Those who themselves have caused the weakening of the foundations of the non-proliferation regime must answer this question; not only in Iran, but in the entire region and globally," said Baghaei. Responding to reports that the pre-war "Cairo Agreement", a framework negotiated between Iran's Foreign Minister and the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) chief, could serve as a roadmap to break the deadlock, Baghaei signalled that the window for that arrangement had closed. "The Cairo Agreement, which is now part of history, the opposing parties did not really appreciate its opportunity," said Baghaei. Regarding third-party mediation, while Russian President Vladimir Putin discussed the Iranian nuclear situation with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and subsequently US President Donald Trump, Baghaei reiterated the established official channels for US-Iran communications. "We have always welcomed the wonderful efforts of friendly countries; But as you know, technically and in the strict sense of the word, Pakistan and Qatar continue to play the role of mediator between Iran and the United States," added Baghaei. The spokesperson's remarks follow parallel political developments. Russian President Vladimir Putin stressed during discussions that "the scope for diplomacy on Iran is far from exhausted" and called an agreement both possible and necessary. US President Donald Trump noted that the conflict with Iran would conclude "very soon," either through continued military pressure or an agreement on Washington's terms, reiterating that "Iran will never have a nuclear weapon". Iran’s Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei stated that while the US addressed some of Iran's seven conditions regarding the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, Washington's overall response remained "inadequate". (ANI)

stories.title: INDIA Bloc Marches To Supreme Court; CJI Declines Meet; CEC Dismissal Sought
stories.summary: INDIA Bloc Marches To Supreme Court; CJI Declines Meet; CEC Dismissal Sought
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

article_sentences: Rahul Gandhi and 10 INDIA bloc leaders seek a halt to SIR, safeguards against voter deletions, public disclosure of records and an independent audit.

The INDIA bloc has asked the Supreme Court to suspend the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, prevent voter deletions without a hearing and order an independent audit of changes made to voter lists.

Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and 10 other INDIA bloc leaders filed a petition against the Election Commission of India (ECI), challenging the way it made decisions related to the revision exercise.
The plea also seeks the disclosure of internal records and greater transparency in decisions affecting electoral rolls.
The petition was filed as Opposition leaders arrived at the Supreme Court after marching through central Delhi.
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge confirmed the filing, while RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav said the Opposition was fighting to save democracy.
What are the INDIA bloc’s demands?
The Opposition has asked the court to suspend the ongoing Special Intensive Revision process until it decides the case.
The petition seeks a direction that no elector should be removed from the electoral roll without prior notice and a reasonable opportunity to be heard in accordance with the law.
The INDIA bloc wants the ECI to publish booth-wise lists of deleted electors, along with the reasons for their removal and demographic details.
The plea seeks the Election Commission’s complete files, agendas, minutes, internal notings and objections relating to disputed decisions, including the June 24, 2025, decision to begin the SIR.
The petition asks for an independent committee headed by a retired Supreme Court judge to audit deletions and modifications in electoral-roll databases, including ECINET and ERONET.

stories.title: President appoints 4 new state governors; switches governors for 2 states
stories.summary: Keralam Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar has been appointed as the Governor of Tamil Nadu, as part of a major gubernatorial reshuffle effected by President Droupadi Murmu on Monday. Om Prakash Mathur, Governor of Sikkim, will be the new Governor of Keralam in place of Arlekar, a communique issued by the Rashtrapati Bhavan said. Dushyant Gautam has been appointed the Governor of Sikkim, it said. Senior BJP leader from Jharkhand, Braj Mohan Ram, has been appointed as the Governor of Odisha. Sudha Yadav has been named the Governor of Karnataka and Dhal Singh Bisen will be Uttarakhand Governor, the communique said. These appointments will take effect from the dates they will assume charge of their respective offices, it added.

stories.title: Madhur Bhandarkar to lead Feature Film jury at 57th Indian Panorama
stories.summary: Mumbai, Oct 12 : Filmmaker Madhur Bhandarkar, who is known for ‘Chandni Bar’, ‘Page 3’, ‘Fashion’, and ‘Babli Bouncer’, has been appointed as the Chairman of the Jury for the Feature Film Section of Indian Panorama for the upcoming 57th edition of the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026. As Chairman of the Feature Film Jury, he will be responsible for evaluating eligible entries and recommending 25 outstanding feature films for showcase at the 57th IFFI. This selection will include five films from mainstream cinema recommended by designated film trade bodies. The festival primarily comprises two major sections, International Cinema and Indian Panorama. The Indian Panorama is a flagship section dedicated to showcasing the best of contemporary Indian cinema and promoting excellence in filmmaking. The official communication was issued by Ashutosh Gowariker, Festival Director of the 57th IFFI. The film festival, which is organised by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India, the International Film Festival of India has been celebrating cinema from across the world since its inception in 1952. From the selected films, the jury will recommend three films for the main competition, two films for the Best Debut Film of a Director category, and three films for the ICFT UNESCO-Gandhi Medal under the international competition. The jury will also evaluate entries for the Best Debut Director of Indian Feature Film Award, recommending five films and selecting the winner. The primary jury screening of eligible feature film entries commenced online on September 29 and is scheduled to continue until October 16, 2026. This will be followed by the central panel jury screening of 60 shortlisted feature films at the NFDC Auditorium in Mumbai from October 18 to November 1, 2026. The 57th edition of IFFI is set to be held from November 20 to November 28, 2026 in Goa. --IANS

stories.headline: Anti-CEC row updates: INDIA bloc leads march through Delhi, takes SIR protest to Supreme Court
stories.title: Anti-CEC row updates: INDIA bloc leads march through Delhi, takes SIR protest to Supreme Court
stories.summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convener Saurav Das on Monday (October 12, 2026) said the government’s decision to denotify Jantar Mantar as a protest site is “unacceptable”
reasons: source: event has 3 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 3 independent source groups -> high confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: President of the Indian National Congress Mallikarjun Kharge, wearing a Batman mask, sits next to Congress leader and Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi as opposition parties march to the Supreme Court in Delhi, India, October 12, 2026.
On a day when Delhi.

Police denotified Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site, a sizeable crowd walked down arterial roads in the capital, tailing a procession of buses carrying leaders of the Indian National Developmental, Inclusive Alliance (INDIA) from Constitution Club to the Supreme Court, where Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabh Rahul Gandhi and other top leaders of the coalition filed a petition over the alleged large-scale voter deletions and irregularities in the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
After winding through central Delhi and doubling back via Mandi House, the procession was finally stopped by the police near the Supreme Court.

Several leaders, including Mr. Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Tejashwi Yadav and Akhilesh Yadav, climbed atop a vehicle for the last leg of the march, which rang with slogans against the government and the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar.
Several top Congress leaders, including Sachin Pilot, were seen marching along with the protesters.

The final electoral rolls of all 117 Assembly constituencies were published on Monday (October 12, 2026) following the completion of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in Punjab, and the names of around 13.60 lakh people went unrecorded as a result of permanent relocation, absence, death or duplicate entries.
Punjab final electoral rolls show 2.01 crore voters after SIR, with 13.6 lakh names dropped due to relocation, death, absence, or duplicates.
In the aftermath of the Opposition march to the Supreme Court in Delhi, Assam CM in a press conference alleged that Rahul Gandhi, and the Congress party is being guided by foreign forces.
“They don’t like this country’s Supreme Court, Election Commission, or the Parliament,” he said.
Congress president and Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge was seen donning a Batman mask during INDIA bloc’s march to SC.
Bus with INDIA Bloc leaders turned towards Copernicus Marg (leading to India Gate circle).

stories.headline: Supreme Court wants cap on trade margin for all essential medicines and medical products
stories.title: Supreme Court wants cap on trade margin for all essential medicines and medical products
stories.summary: Government proposes 30% trade-margin cap on patented and non-patented cancer medicines, but top court asks why a margin cap cannot be extended to all medicines and medical products; the court says the government has to ensure that DPCO-approved medicines, whose price is legally regulated, reach patients
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Even as the Centre informed the Supreme Court on Monday (October 12, 2026) that it had decided to cap trade margins at 30% for non-scheduled cancer drugs, the court questioned why the benefit of such price regulation should be confined to cancer drugs and not extended to other essential medicines and medical products.

The development comes after a Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta expressed concern over stark disparities between the price to retailer (PTR) and the maximum retail price (MRP) of certain medicines, particularly cancer drugs, with mark-ups in some instances soaring to 1,000%.
The Bench had flagged that such exorbitant mark-ups constituted “broad daylight dacoity” and placed an enormous financial burden on patients.

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre, informed the Bench that the proposed 30% trade-margin cap would cover both patented and non-patented cancer medicines, with an expert committee headed by the Director General of Health Services tasked with identifying the drugs to be brought within its ambit.
The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) will examine the committee’s recommendations before issuing a price notification to implement the cap.

The Bench, however, said that while the intervention was commendable, it was inadequate, and questioned why other medicines and medical devices could not also be brought within the 16% retailer margin prescribed under the Drugs (Prices Control) Order (DPCO), 2013.
“This is just the tip of the iceberg...
this has come around only because of the unduly hard observations we made during earlier hearings.
What about other drugs,” the Bench asked.

The top court was hearing petitions filed by advocate Kishan Chand Jain and paediatric surgeon Sanjay Kulshrestha seeking stricter enforcement of price controls under the DPCO to curb disproportionate margins across the pharmaceutical supply chain.

Justice Mehta drew attention to steep markups on medical devices and consumables, pointing out that an India-made cardiac stent costing around ₹5,000 was being sold by hospitals for more than ₹25,000.
He cited the example of a saline drip line carrying an MRP of ₹11 being sold for ₹270.

stories.headline: Rahul Gandhi & INDIA Bloc Leaders File Writ Petition In Supreme Court Against ECI Over SIR Process
stories.title: Rahul Gandhi & INDIA Bloc Leaders File Writ Petition In Supreme Court Against ECI Over SIR Process
stories.summary: They have sought the suspension of SIR process.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi has filed a writ petition in the Supreme Court challenging the Election Commission of India's (ECI) Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

The petition comes amid the Congress-led Opposition's protests against the SIR exercise and seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the alleged irregularities in the voters' roll revision.
Ahead of filing the petition, Gandhi, along with Congress and other Opposition leaders, led a march towards the Supreme Court on Monday (October 12).

The development comes a day after Chief Justice of India Surya Kant declined Gandhi's request for an appointment to discuss issues relating to the SIR exercise and the functioning of the Election Commission.

Gandhi and Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge, who is the Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, had sought a meeting with the CJI to submit a memorandum raising concerns over the SIR process and demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
The CJI declined the request, stating that the issues sought to be raised were already pending before the Supreme Court.

He also conveyed that the Court could not interfere with the functioning of the government on its administrative side, while clarifying that the leaders were free to approach the Court on its judicial side for appropriate relief.
Similar matters concerning the SIR exercise are scheduled to be heard by the Supreme Court on Tuesday.
The CJI had indicated that any petition filed by the Opposition leaders could also be considered along with the pending matters.
Further details of the prayers and grounds raised in Gandhi's writ petition are awaited.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Bar Association & SCAORA Condemn Calls For CJI Surya Kant's Resignation
stories.title: Supreme Court Bar Association & SCAORA Condemn Calls For CJI Surya Kant's Resignation
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) and the Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association (SCAORA) have condemned statements circulated on social media seeking the resignation of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant, stating that such remarks belittle the institution of the judiciary and amount to an attempt to interfere with the administration of justice.
In a resolution dated October 12, 2026, the SCBA said that every person has the opportunity to approach the courts and seek remedies in accordance with law.
"Statements of this nature belittle the institution of the judiciary and amounts to an attempt to interfere with the administration of justice," the resolution stated.
The Bar Association called upon its members and all other individuals to maintain the dignity and decorum of the Supreme Court of India.
The resolution was signed by SCBA Honorary Secretary Pragya Baghel.
The Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association (SCAORA) has expressed strong disapproval of statements made in the public domain seeking the resignation of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant.
In a resolution dated October 12, 2026, SCAORA said that the judiciary is a constitutional institution entrusted with upholding the rule of law and protecting the rights of citizens.
It said that any grievance concerning judicial functioning must be raised through appropriate legal and constitutional channels.
"Public statements seeking the resignation of the head of the judiciary risk undermining the dignity of the office and public confidence in the institution," the resolution stated.
SCAORA urged all concerned to respect the independence of the judiciary and maintain the dignity and decorum of the Supreme Court of India.
"The judicial process must be allowed to function independently, without pressure or interference," it added.
The SCAORA resolution was signed by its Honorary Secretary, Yugandhara Pawar Jha.

stories.headline: Supreme Court asks why drug margin caps cannot cover all medicines
stories.title: Supreme Court asks why drug margin caps cannot cover all medicines
stories.summary: The court cited steep markups on medical products as the Centre outlined existing price-control rules and defended its approach to medicine pricing
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday said the Centre’s response on capping the trade margin of anti-cancer drugs at 30 per cent of the maximum retail price (MRP) is “hardly anything to be happy about” and questioned why the government cannot cap trade margins of other medicines.

The Centre, which has earlier come under severe criticism from the top court for steep markup of cancer drugs by hospitals, said that the government has taken an important decision to cap the trade margin on anti-cancer drugs at 30 per cent of the MRP, which is expected to result in annual savings of approximately Rs 2,500 crore to patients.
A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta said that the Centre’s response was insufficient and flagged that a single saline drip was sold in market for Rs 270 while its actual cost was Rs 11.
“There is hardly anything to be happy about.

There is actually nothing for the benefit of the patients,” the bench observed as Solicitor General Tushar Mehta and Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre, tried to explain the regime in place.

Mehta said that the government has taken an important step to cap the trade margin on anti-cancer drugs at 30 per cent of the MRP, which would result in savings of approximately Rs 2,500 crore to patients.

Justice Nath told the solicitor general that the court fails to understand that if the government can cap the price of anti-cancer drugs, then why can it not bring all the medicines under this regime.
“We understand that there are transportation costs, raw material cost, R&D cost and all other ancillary costs, but all these are included in the MRP.
What is the logic behind allowing them to sell 400 times the actual cost?
How can you allow this?” the bench observed.
Bhati said that the cost of medicines in India was the lowest in the world and that is the reason a lot of people come to the country for treatment.

Justice Mehta said that the cost of an India-made cardiac stent is around Rs 5,000 but it is sold by hospitals for more than Rs 25,000 and similarly, the cost of common antibiotic Azithromycin is sold at over Rs 70 while its actual cost is around Rs 28.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Issues Notice On PIL Seeking Proper Maintenance Of Accessible Airport Infrastructure
stories.title: Supreme Court Issues Notice On PIL Seeking Proper Maintenance Of Accessible Airport Infrastructure
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court recently issued notice on a PIL seeking proper maintenance of accessible airport infrastructure, including tactile pathways, Braille signage, accessible seating, and priority check-in for persons with disabilities.

A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana called for the responses of the Ministry of Civil Aviation, the Directorate General of Civil Aviation, the Airport Authority of India, the Central Industrial Security Force and the Digi Yatra Foundation.

The public interest litigation, filed by one Turab Chimthanawala, challenges "systemic and continuing failure" on the part of respondent-authorities in ensuring and operationalizing the accessibility standards and regulatory mandates governing civil aviation in India, including the Accessibility Standards and Guidelines for Civil Aviation 2022, Rule 15(1)(f) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Rules 2017, the Civil Aviation Requirements titled "Carriage by Air-Persons with Disability (Divyangjan) and/or Persons with Reduced Mobility" (PRM-CAR) issued by the DGCA.

He claims that despite a comprehensive statutory and regulatory framework, there is complete absence of a proper monitoring mechanism that would ensure implementation of the 2022 Standards and Guidelines and the PRM-CAR.

"This systemic failure has resulted in continuing and widespread inaccessibility across civil aviation infrastructure and services, including inaccessible airport infrastructure, lack of accessible signage and navigation systems, absence of accessible digital and biometric systems such as DigiYatra, inaccessible booking and check-in systems, improper handling of mobility aids, lack of trained personnel, coercive or inappropriate assistance practices, and the absence of dignified and accessible screening and immigration procedures.
These failures constitute a continuing violation of statutory mandates as well as the fundamental rights of PwDs."
The petitioner seeks enforcement of fundamental rights of persons with disabilities, including their Right to Accessibility, an integral part of Articles 14, 19(1)(d) and 21 of the Constitution.
He avers that the State and its instrumentalities have a "non-derogable obligation" to ensure that public infrastructure and services are usable by PwDs on an equal basis with others.
The petition has been drawn by Advocates Rahul Bajaj, Amar Jain, Sarah and Amritesh Mishra, and filed through AoR Ashutosh Senger.
